cast.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair

personas.name: Bernadette
personas.hidden_agenda: Knows a councillor personally but doesn't want to look like she's using it

personas.name: Cyril
personas.hidden_agenda: His late wife's roses are on plot 3

personas.name: Amara
personas.hidden_agenda: Has already talked to a local reporter

personas.name: Felipe
personas.goals: A plan that doesn't bankrupt the association
personas.hidden_agenda: Thinks the rent increase is actually survivable

agenda.title: The lease
agenda.goal: Respond to the city's lease proposal

agenda.title: The campaign
agenda.goal: Plan the petition and the council meeting

agenda.title: Spring fair
agenda.goal: Decide whether the fair goes ahead

beats.summary: The city's proposal; tempers; Felipe overstates the increase and is corrected later
Petition and council; Amara's count is high

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Thank you for coming at short notice. The city wants a new lease from July, and the rent goes up.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: The rent's doubling. That's what the letter says.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: Doubling! After all these years. We've been on this site fifty years.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: This is exactly what they do. Squeeze community spaces until they give up.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: The current lease ends June thirtieth. We have until then to respond.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: We respond by fighting them. Every one of us.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: Fighting costs money. A lawyer just to read the lease is six hundred.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Six hundred is nothing compared to losing the allotments.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: My wife planted those roses on plot three. I'm not handing them to a car park.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Nobody's handing anything to anybody, Cyril.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: I've already talked to a reporter at the Gazette. She's interested.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Before we'd even met as a committee?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Someone had to do something.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: I've got the letter here, sorry. It's not doubling. It's a sixty percent increase. I misread the table.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: Sixty percent. That's still robbery.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: The current rent is twenty-four hundred a year. Sixty percent more is about thirty-eight hundred.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Then we spend six hundred on the lawyer, and we make our case before we sign anything.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: I'll book the lawyer for next week.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: The petition is at about two thousand signatures already. People really care.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Two thousand online, or on paper?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Well, about eight hundred and thirty verified. The rest are shares and likes.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: Eight hundred and thirty real signatures is still impressive.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: When is the council meeting?

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: April ninth. Public comments are allowed.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Then we fill the room. Fifty-eight plot holders, forty-one on the waitlist, their families.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: I'll speak. I've earned it.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Cyril, you'll speak from the heart, which is good. But someone needs to speak to the numbers too.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: I can do the numbers. Calmly.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: And I'll organize who sits where, so it looks like a crowd and not a rabble.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Should I mention that I know Councillor Pryce?

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: The council parking lot is always full on meeting nights. Last time I parked three streets away and got a ticket.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: Did you appeal it?

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: Of course I appealed. I lost.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: The campaign, everyone, please.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: Money. We have sixty-two hundred in the account.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: Then we can afford to fight.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: We can afford a lawyer and the new rent for a year. Not a long legal battle.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Could we ask for donations alongside the petition?

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: We can, but we have to account for every penny.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Then a donation link goes on the petition, and Felipe keeps a separate record.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: The water bill was nineteen hundred last year. That doesn't go away either.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Maybe we propose a lower increase and offer to maintain the park strip next to us in return.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Let's see what the lawyer says before we offer anything.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: The fair. May twenty-fourth. Do we still hold it?

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: Of course we hold it. Especially now.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: It would show the city what the allotments are for.

turns.speaker: Felipe
turns.text: And bring in money. We'll need it.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: The fair goes ahead, and we make it part of the campaign.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: I'll ask the reporter to come to the fair. That's a much better story than an angry meeting.

turns.speaker: Cyril
turns.text: It would be good if someone made a display of the history. Old photos.

turns.speaker: Bernadette
turns.text: Thank you, all of you. We're not giving up these plots.
